sentences.text: This small fish reached a total length of 25 to 30 cm.
The genus is defined by prominent fin spines that curve forward over the animal's head.
Males possessed a prominent dorsal fin spine covered in denticles, while females lacked these structures.
The species was originally described in 1883 from the St. Louis Limestone under the name Physonemus falcatus.
In 1985, fossils from Montana were described that revealed a high degree of sexual dimorphism in the genus.
Falcatus was a predator that fed on shrimp.
Many fossils show distended gills, suggesting they died from asphyxiation in oxygen-poor waters.
Falcatus lived during the early Carboniferous Period in Bear Gulch Bay, now located in Montana.
It lived between 330.3 and 323.4 million years ago during the Serpukhovian stage.
Fossils of Falcatus have been found in Montana and Missouri, USA.
It is debated whether Falcatus died from asphyxiation in oxygen-poor waters or was rapidly buried by mudslides caused by heavy rainfall.
